Hi Marissa / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We had a good discussion internally and the execs are comfortable moving forward with a short POC to validate latency, cost, and answer a few integration questions.

High-level goals / success criteria from our side:
- Validate 99th percentile latency under our peak traffic for a representative workload (see rough numbers below)
- Verify cost per 1M tokens projection within 20% of Redwood's estimate
- Confirm that the model outputs match our safety/evaluation tests (we'll provide test prompts)
- End-to-end integration proof: auth, request routing, and logging into our telemetry

Initial timeline: 3-week POC (start as early as 3/8), org sign-off by 3/31 if results look good.

Workload summary (very approximate):
- Typical concurrent sessions: 150-250 (mostly web/REST clients)
- Average incoming request rate: 40 req/s steady-state, with bursts up to ~120 req/s for a few 5–10 minute windows during peak hours
- Token lengths: user prompt ~20-80 tokens; model response ~60-250 tokens (longer for some batch summaries)
- Target RPS per user request: 1–2 calls in quick succession for multi-turn flows

We can pull sample logs and a short CSV with timestamps if that helps. Can you send your workload intake template and a proposed evaluation plan with ownership and milestones? Also please call out any infra requirements (VPC, egress, certs) we should start prepping.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan

Hi Priya — quick technical follow-ups to help size the POC and pick defaults:

1) When you list token lengths, do your token counts include system/instruction tokens or should we plan for user+assistant only? (affects cost projection)
2) For the burst windows (120 req/s for 5–10m), is that across all endpoints or concentrated on a single route? Any per-route SLAs we should be aware of?
3) Concurrency pattern: are the 150–250 concurrent sessions long-lived websockets (with KV cache reuse) or short REST calls? If long-lived we can enable prefix/KV cache which reduces cost & latency.
4) Do you expect streaming responses for the long summaries or prefer full-response mode? Streaming changes resource allocation a bit.

If you can reply with the above, I can pre-config an initial cluster profile (batching thresholds, cache TTLs) and include our recommended model variant/quantization profile for cost.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Token counts include system + user.
- Bursts are concentrated on the /summarize endpoint (we send a lot of batch jobs at 09:00 & 17:00 local time).
- Sessions are mostly short REST requests; we do have an internal worker that runs longer multi-turn flows (~5% of traffic) that could benefit from KV caching.
